Create a BayesTraits project folder with associated example scripts and input data for a full shell script run and log processing of BayesTraits phylogenetic regression analyses

Source: R/shell_phyreg_proj.R
shell.phyreg.proj.Rd

By reporting a directory path and the computer's operating system ("unix" or "windows"), this function creates a BayesTraits project folder with associated example scripts and input data for a full shell script run and log processing of multiple phylogenetic regression analyses with Meade & Pagel's (2022) BayesTraits program. The function produces an example of a shell script in Unix or Windows PowerShell that helps to fully automate both the complete BayesTraits regression analysis and the processing of the resulting log and stones files, by automatically running the three main InNOutBT functions phyreg.inputs, phyreg.shell, and phyreg.outputs, without directly opening the R or RStudio programs. Note that these files are just examples from a specific study of the Vataireoid legumes, and so you will have to edit the folder paths and analysis parameters in these example scripts according to your desired regression analyses. See also a more complete article describing a BayesTraits shell run project that can be created with shell.phyreg.proj for fully automated multiple phylogenetic regression analyses.

Usage

shell.phyreg.proj(dir_create_proj = NULL,
                  syst = NULL)

Arguments

dir_create_proj

Path to any directory on your computer where an example of a BayesTraits shell project folder and associated files for a full run with shell script should be saved.

syst

Report the operating system ("unix" or "windows").

Details

After creating the project folder with this function, follow these steps to run the project. These steps are for macOS (syst = "unix"); see the article linked above for the steps in Windows PowerShell.

Before the first run

  1. Install the BayesTraits program in any folder and note the path to that folder and the name of the executable file (e.g., BayesTraitsV5).

  2. Check that the executable file starts by running its full path in the Terminal. If macOS stops it (e.g., the message killed), remove the block that macOS adds to downloaded files, provided that you trust the source of the download: xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /path/to/BayesTraits/BayesTraitsV5.

  3. Check that the R packages InNOutBT and treeio are installed, and that pandoc is available in the Terminal, as the Word table needs it: Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::pandoc_available()'.

Edit the project files in any text editor

  1. In BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh, set PROJECTFOLDER to the path of the project folder, BAYESTRFOLDER to the path of the folder that contains the BayesTraits executable file, and EMAIL to your e-mail address.

  2. In 2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R, set BayesTraits_dir to the same path as BAYESTRFOLDER, and BayesTraits_exe to the name of the executable file.

  3. To run your own study, also edit the three numbered R scripts and replace the files in the Data folder.

Run the project in the Terminal

  1. Move to the project folder, not to the BayesTraits folder, because the main shell script moves to the BayesTraits folder by itself: cd /path/to/BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project.

  2. Allow the main shell script to run, which is needed only once: chmod 777 BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh.

  3. Start the full analysis: ./BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh. Keep the Terminal open until it finishes, which can take a long time with the default number of iterations.

The script then produces the input files, creates and runs the BayesTraits analyses, moves the resulting log and stones files to the project folder, and processes them. The final table and heatmaps are saved in the project folder, in results_BayesTraits_phyreg_output, within a subfolder named with the current date.

library(InNOutBT)

shell.phyreg.proj(dir_create_proj = "/Users/domingoscardoso",
